sections.html:
Windsor is a Hartford County town on the northern border of Hartford, and it was the first English settlement in Connecticut. It covers about 31.0 square miles, of which 29.5 are land, and the 2020 census counted 29,492 residents.

The Connecticut River forms its eastern edge, and the Farmington River joins the larger river inside the town. Bloomfield lies to the west, East Granby to the northwest, Windsor Locks to the north and South Windsor and East Windsor across the river. The ZIP code is 06095.

The terrain is low. The town's highest point is Day Hill at 230 feet, and the lowest is the river itself at 5 feet. A seller near the river should ask the town and FEMA about the parcel's flood zone, because buyers and their lenders will.

sections.h2: What are the villages inside Windsor?
sections.html:
Windsor is made up of several named communities rather than one grid. The principal communities named on Wikipedia are Deerfield, Hayden Station, Poquonock, Rainbow, Wilson and Windsor Center.

  • Windsor Center, with the train station and the Shad Derby Festival each spring
  • Poquonock, which has its own elementary school
  • Wilson, in the south of town near Hartford, named for a landowner who gave the railroad right of way
  • Hayden Station, in the north, named the same way
  • Rainbow, a northern section of town; the Farmington River is dammed in the northwest corner to form the 234 acre Rainbow Reservoir

When you describe a house to a buyer, naming the village helps.

sections.h2: What is Windsor's history, and does it show up in house sales?
sections.html:
Windsor's first English party, led by William Holmes, arrived on September 26, 1633 and founded a trading post at the meeting of the Farmington and Connecticut Rivers. The settlement was renamed Windsor on February 21, 1637, the day it was incorporated with Hartford and Wethersfield.

The first highway in the Connecticut Colony opened in 1638 between Windsor and Hartford. Many later towns were carved out of Windsor's original boundaries, including East Windsor, South Windsor, Windsor Locks, Bloomfield and Simsbury.

Landmarks include the Oliver Ellsworth Homestead, the home of Oliver Ellsworth, third Chief Justice of the United States, and a restored train station dating to the 1850s. From 1957 to 2006 the town also hosted the S1C Nuclear Powered Training Unit, a Navy prototype plant. Its site became the first nuclear reactor site released for unrestricted use after demolition and decontamination. A buyer who asks about industrial land use near your street deserves a straight answer, and the town's planning office can supply it.

sections.h2: What is the economy of Windsor, and who are the big employers?
sections.html:
Windsor's largest employer by far is Amazon, with 7,223 employees according to the town's 2025 annual financial report as summarized on Wikipedia. The town government comes second.

RankEmployerEmployees
1Amazon.com7,223
2Town of Windsor1,181
3Voya Financial723
4Walgreens650
5SS & C Technologies500
6Target Distribution Center460
7Dollar Tree426
8Eversource Energy400

The list is heavy on distribution and logistics, which fits the town's location beside Bradley International Airport and on Interstate 91. Agriculture once carried the economy. Connecticut shade tobacco, grown for cigar wrappers, was a major local crop, and about 34,000 acres of Connecticut soil is mapped as Windsor soil, named after the town.

sections.h2: How do people get around Windsor?
sections.html:
Windsor has more transportation options than most Connecticut suburbs. Interstate 91 and Interstate 291 cross town, and Bradley International Airport borders it.

  • Interstates 91 and 291
  • State routes 20, 75, 159, 178, 187, 218 and 305
  • Windsor station, served by the CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak
  • CT Transit bus service

The station sits in the former Hartford and New Haven Railroad depot, and the Hartford Line double track was restored in 2018. The old trolley that ran to Hartford stopped in 1940. For commuters, that rail link is the selling point you can lead with, because it gives buyers an alternative to Interstate 91 traffic.

sections.h2: What are Windsor's schools and parks?
sections.html:
Windsor Public Schools operate Clover Street School, John F. Kennedy School, Oliver Ellsworth School, Poquonock School, Sage Park Middle School and Windsor High School. The Capitol Region Education Council also runs aerospace and engineering academies for middle and high school students.

Private options include the Loomis Chaffee School, whose fields sit on the site of the original 1633 trading post, Saint Gabriel's School for kindergarten through eighth grade, and Madina Academy.

The park system is a genuine draw. Northwest Park covers 473 acres with a nature center and trails, Windsor Meadows State Park runs along the Connecticut River, and Keney Park has a golf course and cricket fields. The Mill Brook Open Space is a 95 acre property used for recreation, wildlife habitat and stormwater protection. Mentioning the closest park to your address is a useful line in any listing or offer conversation.

sections.h2: Why do some Windsor houses sell slowly?
sections.html:
Common reasons are age, deferred maintenance and a location near the river or the interstates. Windsor's population jumped from 10,068 in 1940 to 19,467 in 1960 and 25,204 in 1980, so a large share of its housing was likely built in those decades.

Houses of that age can need new roofs or heating systems, and a buyer using a mortgage may ask for that work before closing. The 2010 census counted 11,767 housing units in town.

If a roof replacement, a heating system or a foundation repair stands between you and a listing, an as-is cash sale removes that step. Compare the offer to a listing's net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs, not to the headline list price.

sections.h2: How does a sale close in Windsor, and what does the state require?
sections.html:
Every Connecticut deed transfer triggers a state conveyance tax return, and the seller's side files it. The Department of Revenue Services requires Form OP-236 from the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an agent when the price is $2,000 or more, unless an exemption applies.

QuestionAnswer from the state's page
Who filesGrantor, grantor's attorney or authorized agent
WhenWhen the deed is recorded
Threshold$2,000 or more in consideration
Windsor town code on the form164
Electronic optionmyCTREC, in participating towns

One exemption matters to stressed sellers. A principal residence sold for less than the mortgages plus priority real estate taxes and municipal liens can be exempt from the state tax. Ask your attorney whether it applies to your sale.

sections.h2: What should Windsor owners check with the town about property taxes?
sections.html:
Ask the town's assessor and tax collector for the current mill rate, any revaluation phase-in and the status of your tax bills. We did not confirm those figures from an opened town page, so we do not state them here.

That matters at closing. Unpaid property tax and any municipal liens are paid from the sale proceeds, and a closing attorney will order a tax status check. Connecticut's local tax statutes also let a municipality add certain code enforcement expenses to the tax bill of a property that violates health, safety or housing codes, so ask whether any such charge is attached to your parcel.

Sellers should also ask whether any veteran, elderly or disability relief they qualify for was applied. State law lets an owner who later obtains proof of an exemption request an abatement or refund, but only within one year of getting that proof.

faqs.a: Windsor covers about 31.0 square miles, with 29.5 square miles of land, and had 29,492 residents in the 2020 census. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 29,879.

faqs.q: What is the biggest employer in Windsor?
faqs.a: Amazon, with 7,223 employees in the town's 2025 annual financial report. The Town of Windsor is second with 1,181 employees.

faqs.q: Is there train service in Windsor?
faqs.a: Yes. Windsor station is served by the CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak's Northeast Regional and Valley Eagle trains.
The town's principal communities are Deerfield, Hayden Station, Poquonock, Rainbow, Wilson and Windsor Center.

faqs.q: What is the Windsor code on the state conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue Services lists 164 as Windsor's town code on Form OP-236. The seller's side files the return when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Windsor house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A mortgage-financed buyer may demand repairs, while a cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands.
